newsitem.title: LATVIA: Baltic cooperation said key to Europe stability.
newsitem.headline: Baltic cooperation said key to Europe stability.

text.p: The Council of the Baltic Sea States, a regional cooperation body, expressed the belief at the end of a ministerial meeting on Thursday that stronger ties in the strategic region were important for for European stability as a whole.
The foreign ministers of most of the countries that surround the Baltic Sea, including Germany, Poland and the Nordic and Baltic states, met for two days in the Latvian capital, Riga.
Russia sent a deputy foreign minister, Alexander Avdeyev.
The eastern shore of the Baltic sea is dominated by former Communist-bloc nations which are trying hard to reintegrate with the West and catch up economically with their richer neighbours.

A joint communique said the participants "expressed their firm belief that a strengthening of co-operation in the entire Baltic Sea area will substantially contribute to the creation of a stable, democratic, prosperous and undivided Europe".
The ministers also stressed the importance of the eastward enlargement of the 15-member European Union.
Swedish Foreign Minister Lena Hjelm-Wallen said the EU issue was widely discussed at the meeting.

"From our side, we are pressing very much for a simulataneous start to talks on membership. I am rather optimistic we will have a simultaneous start," she told a news conference. Sweden is a member of the EU.
Poland and the three Baltic states have all applied for full membership of the EU but are expected eventually to get into the trading bloc in different stages.
The EU's executive Commission will in two weeks unveil its assessment on how suitable 10 former Soviet bloc countries are for EU membership.
